_comment: Which PADI Travel vessel is which of ours. Hand-maintained, one deliberate
call per entry, because similarity on vessel names ranks garbage above
truth here: 'Destiny' scores 0.67 against PADI's 'eriny' while the real
'New Sambo' -> 'new-sambo-safari-boat-2' pair scores 0.59. No threshold
separates those two, so there is no automatic version of this file.
Boats whose folded names already agree need no entry -- they resolve on
their own. This file is for the exceptions and, with equal weight, for the
boats confirmed absent: a boat reviewed and found not to be on PADI is a
different state from one nobody has looked at, and only writing both down
stops the tail being re-reviewed every time.
PADI slugs are ids and nothing more -- see docs/sources/padi.com.md on why
an itinerary slug contradicts its own page 15 times out of 22. The same
caution applies here: a vessel slug is not evidence of the vessel's name.

Keyed on our boat_id, not on the boat's name. 'MY Odyssey Liveaboard' has boat_id 'odyssey', and keying on a folded name got that entry wrong on the first attempt -- the id is what promote() builds every itinerary id from, so it is the thing that cannot quietly drift.
Amelie -> amelie-safari, new-sambo -> new-sambo-safari-boat-2 and odyssey ->
my-odyssey were here and were wrong. They came from substring containment,
which looked stronger than similarity scoring and is not: sharing a word with
a vessel's name says nothing about being that vessel. Every entry below is
confirmed against hull facts -- shop kind, country, trip lengths, ports --
and never against a name alone.
amelie-safari (PADI id 18156, 6 cabins) and amelie-adventures (id 93484, 8
cabins) are two different hulls under one operator, confirmed by the fleet
owner. Both are kind 10 and both sell a 3-night Best of Hurghada, so the
cabin count is the only thing that tells them apart -- 6 against our Amelie's
6, 8 against Amelie Adventures' 8. Two boats sharing a name, an operator and
an itinerary is the case a name-based match cannot survive.
odyssey -> my-odyssey was held back for several rounds after an early
name-based guess was rejected, and confirmed on evidence instead: six exact
trip joins, the distinctive Premium Expedition at 10 nights on both sides,
and PADI's 'BDE' being our 'Brothers - Daedalus - Elphinstone'. Its cabin
count is one short of ours, which is the noise the fleet owner said to
expect on specs.
Cabin counts disagree on six of these pairs by one or two -- Topaz 14/16,
Serenity 10/12, Unity 13/14, Ghazala Explorer 13/12, Emperor Asmaa 9/10,
odyssey 14/13 -- and the fleet owner accepted all six: two sources counting a
crew berth differently. Do not 'fix' our figure to match theirs, and do not
reopen these pairs on the strength of the delta alone. The reason a small
delta still gets read rather than waved through is the two Amelies, which are
genuinely different hulls two cabins apart.

'absent' is ours: boats we carry that no PADI record was found for, after probing seven slug shapes each. Accepted as it stands rather than left blank, because vessel_for() cannot tell an unreviewed boat from a reviewed one and a tail that reads as unfinished gets re-walked every time somebody looks.

'unlisted' is gone. It held PADI's side -- boats they sell that we do not carry -- and every one of its 24 entries has now been fetched, so there is nothing left in it to describe. Two were never PADI's side at all: my-avo is our AVO and my-blue is our Blue, and both sat outside 'aliases' and 'absent' alike, which is the one state this file exists to make impossible. Confirmed the way every other pair here was -- on trips, not on names: PADI's 'Daedalus & Elphinstone (Port Ghalib - Port Ghalib)' is byte-identical to AVO's only trip, and Blue matches on two independently. The name agreeing as well is the weakest evidence in the file.

'padi_only' is the other 22: Egyptian liveaboards PADI sells sailings for and liveaboard.com does not. Sailings, not vessels -- and the difference matters. Ten of the 22 have a liveaboard.com fee panel in data/fees.json, so that site carries the boat and simply publishes no departures for it; twelve have no trace there at all. promote() does not need to know which is which: a boat with a fee book uses it like every other boat, and one without falls back to PADI's per-itinerary book. They are in 'aliases' like any other boat, because the mapping is the same mapping -- our boat_id to PADI's slug -- and the id is simply minted here rather than by the first source. Listed separately so the count stays visible: a sailing with one seller has no second opinion about its price, and that is worth being able to find.
